newsitem.title: USA: Maine unemployment rate falls to 5.1 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Maine unemployment rate falls to 5.1 pct in Sept.

text.p: Maine's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate fell to 5.1 percent in September from 5.5 percent in August, state Labor Commissioner said Monday.
Seasonally adjusted nonfarm wage and salary jobs rose by 1,200 between August and September, with the largest gains in retail trade, services and government, the commissioner's office reported.

There were 600 more nonfarm jobs than in September 1995. Over-the-year the largest increases were in services, retail trade and whoelsale trade. The largest declines were recorded in nondurable goods manufacturing and government.

Other New England states which have reported their seasonally-adjusted umeployment rates include Vermont at 4.4 pecrent, New Hampshire at 4.3 percent and Massachusetts 4.2 percent. The adjusted national rate for September was 5.2 percent.
Maine's not-seasonally adjusted unemployment rate was 4.1 percent in September, down from 4.4 percent in August and 4.7 percent in September 1995.
Not-seasonally adjusted unemployment rates in Maine counties ranged from 2.2 percent in Lincoln County to 7.2 percent in Washington County.
